content:

Subject: Tenant containment strategy — can you share a concise impact summary and diagram?

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Our security review team needs a short, focused summary of how Redwood will contain tenant blast radius during the upcoming migration from our staging tenancy into the Dedicated pool. Specific asks:

- A one-page diagram that shows containment rings and egress choke points during migration (control plane vs data plane).
- A short list of configuration changes that might affect our SLA (connection draining, cache warm-up, routing fallback).
- Any temporary observability gaps and how long they could last.

We'd like to include this in our internal SIG review on Thursday. Can you send by EOD Wednesday PST?

Best,
Alice
Alice Park
Sr. Security Engineer — Veridian Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@veridian.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenant containment strategy — can you share a concise impact summary and diagram?

Alice —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a concise diagram and a migration-impact matrix that maps configuration changes to SLA and observability effects. Short summary below:

1) Containment model (summary)
- Rings: Control Plane (shared control plane in customer-managed VPC mode), Edge Gateways (tenant-specific ALB+egress proxies), Dedicated Enclave (isolated GPU pool).
- During migration we create a temporary overlay: traffic ingress is routed to the target Dedicated Enclave via our staging gateway while the source enclave remains in read-only mode. This avoids cross-tenant KV cache contamination.

2) Egress choke points and mitigations
- Egress is choked at the enclave edge via enforced NAT rules and static egress proxies. We temporarily tighten egress ACLs during live cutover windows; exceptions are tracked and can be rolled back within the SLA window.

3) SLA impact & duration
- Expected brief latency bump for cold-started model instances (median +30–120 ms for affected requests) during prefix cache warm-up.
- Connection draining may extend tail latency up to 500 ms for in-flight requests; overall throughput targets remain intact. Worst-case observable window: 15–45 minutes for the cutover batch.

4) Observability gaps
- Trace sampling for migrations is raised to 100% while the cutover is active; there is a short telemetry lag (up to 60s) as proxies rotate. No logs are dropped; retention and audit trails are preserved.

I've attached: (1) tenant-containment-diagram-v2.png — single-slide visual, and (2) migration-impact-matrix.xlsx — mapping of config changes, rollback steps, and exec owners.

If that looks good I'll turn these into a one-page appendix you can drop into the SIG packet.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Production Security
Redwood Inference

Alice — quick note from the deployment side:

- Migration windows: we recommend a two-phase approach (small pilot cohort, full cohort). Pilot window reduces blast radius and lets us validate egress rules.
- Fallback: our routing fabric supports automated fallback to the previous enclave for up to 30 mins post-cutover; that increases operational churn but keeps user-facing error rate near zero.
- Ops runbook: see the migration-impact-matrix — column G has the exact rollback commands and the runbook step IDs you can reference in your SIG packet.

We'll be available to present the one-slide diagram in the SIG call. Marcus — if you can confirm the expected max telemetry lag I will include a short note on monitoring thresholds.

Thanks,
Marissa
